headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: Flowise can read/write shared files and use broad network egress, while RisingWave is network-isolated and undocumented for pairwise interaction.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read and write the server filesystem and ingest uploaded files; if RisingWave outputs are placed in a shared workspace, Flowise may treat attacker-controlled content as trusted instructions. RisingWave itself has no documented output channel, so the interaction is inferred from Flowise’s file-based ingestion and shared-state deployment model.
conditions: IF RisingWave outputs are written into a directory Flowise reads
IF Flowise flow nodes parse file contents as instructions or prompts
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable file ingestion for untrusted directories
Add provenance tags to all exchanged files
requires-engineering: enforce content-type validation before parsing
requires-engineering: isolate agents with distinct service accounts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and uploaded files, and its network egress is broad, so sensitive data from shared artifacts can leave the workspace. RisingWave is documented as network-egress none, which reduces leakage from B but does not prevent A from exporting data it reads. The pairwise path exists in default deployments if they share files or datastore state.
conditions: IF both agents access the same uploaded files or datastore records
IF Flowise sends file contents to configured model providers or HTTP tools
mitigations: Restrict Flowise to non-sensitive datasets
Turn off or scope HTTP/search tools
Use separate storage buckets per agent
Review outbound destinations in Flowise flows
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on shared storage

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise has filesystem write and broad egress, while RisingWave is non-runnable here with no documented write or network capabilities. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable-resource writes or shared locking, so conflict is limited to unusual deployment choices rather than a default collision.
conditions: IF RisingWave is wrapped by an external service that writes to the same directory as Flowise
IF both agents are granted write access to the same mutable resource
mitigations: Use separate directories and databases
Avoid shared git or filesystem state
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based agent flow builder that can pass outputs into downstream tools, so if RisingWave-derived data is fed into a flow, Flowise may act on it without independent verification. RisingWave has no documented verification or action-taking role here, so the risk is inferred from Flowise’s orchestration behavior rather than direct pairwise evidence.
conditions: IF RisingWave outputs are connected directly into a Flowise node chain
IF Flowise downstream tools execute without a validation step
mitigations: Insert a human review step
Add schema validation between agents
Require citations or checksums on exchanged outputs
Limit downstream actions to read-only previews
requires-engineering: implement verification gates in the flow

E_compliance.rationale: Flowise explicitly handles model provider keys and tool credentials, while RisingWave’s profile does not document regulated-data handling or residency. No specific residency or certification mismatch is evidenced, so compliance risk is limited to documented gaps in Flowise’s secret handling and deployment-dependent storage.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Flowise chatflow inputs or outputs
IF deployment stores secrets or logs in a jurisdiction disallowed by policy
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in Flowise flows
Rotate any exposed credentials
Review logging and retention settings
requires-engineering: document residency and DPA coverage
requires-engineering: segregate regulated workloads
